operations.name: question.create

operations.purpose: Write a question into the bank.

parameters.name: class_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No class matches within the actor's scope.

parameters.notes: The class the question is for. Every question carries one (BR-1, E2).

parameters.name: subject_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No subject matches, or it is not one the actor teaches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the subjects the actor may write for.

parameters.notes: The subject. A teacher works within their own subjects; a Coordinator across their remit (BR-5).

parameters.name: question_type
parameters.type: enum: Multiple choice | True or false | Short answer | Long answer | Numerical
parameters.notes: What kind of question it is. It decides whether options are required (E3).

parameters.name: question_text
parameters.notes: 5 to 2000 characters, as the teacher wrote it. Never rephrased, tidied or translated — a question read differently by a child is a different question.

parameters.name: options
parameters.notes: The choices offered, where the type is multiple choice (E3). The teacher's own, including the wrong ones — a distractor a planner invented is a trap nobody designed.

parameters.name: answer_key
parameters.notes: The correct answer, or the marking points for a written question (BR-1, E1). Never derived from the question — a planner that worked out the answer has set what the school will mark as correct.

parameters.name: marks
parameters.notes: What the question is worth. Greater than zero.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.notes: Optional. Makes the bank searchable by what the question is about (BR-2).

parameters.name: difficulty
parameters.notes: Optional (BR-2). The teacher's judgement, never inferred from the question's wording.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: similar_existing
fields.description: Questions already in the bank for that class and subject with the same topic. Nobody has to rewrite what the school already has.

errors.meaning: A question was saved with no answer key.
errors.note: Without one it cannot be marked (BR-1). Ask the teacher; never derive it.

errors.meaning: A question was saved with no class or subject.
errors.note: Without them it cannot be found again (BR-1).

errors.meaning: A multiple-choice question was saved with no options.
The subject is not one the acting teacher teaches.
errors.note: A teacher works within their own subjects (BR-5).

planningRules.rule: Never write, rephrase or complete the question text. It is what a child reads in an exam hall, and a question a planner tidied is a different question from the one the teacher set.
Never derive the answer key. It is what the school will mark as correct (BR-1), and a planner that worked out the answer has decided that for every student who sits the paper.
Never invent options for a multiple-choice question. The wrong answers are as deliberate as the right one, and a distractor a planner supplied is a trap nobody designed.

Never infer the topic or the difficulty. Both are optional so that a teacher entering a question during a busy week is not blocked by taxonomy (BR-2) — a guess fills the field without anybody deciding it.
Report questions already in the bank on that topic. Nobody should rewrite what the school already has, and that is the whole point of the bank.
Never read a question's text or answer key back to anybody outside the bank's readers. A readable bank is a leaked paper (BR-12).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A question is retired with a reason rather than deleted, and stays attached to the papers that used it (BR-8). There is no delete control (E8).
